newsitem.title: UK: Firmer dollar/mark bolstered by Buba in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Firmer dollar/mark bolstered by Buba in Europe.

text.p: The dollar probed higher against the mark early in Europe, bolstered by comments from Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke that a dollar/mark rate about 1.70 is supported by economic fundamentals.

Traders said the comments from Welteke supported overnight dollar gains against the German unit and combined with rekindled speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve may move to lift interest rates again at its policy-making meeting next week.
Richmond Fed president Alfred Broaddus said late Tuesday the U.S. economy was expanding rapidly and the labour market there will remain tight.
Speaking at a conference in Vienna, Welteke said "It seems that a dollar rate at around 1.70 marks conforms with the real data."
"Welteke is certainly giving the impression the weakness of the mark is not a problem at these levels," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
"Different Buba members have different views on what levels are reasonable but I think there's a consensus that the dollar has not yet posed any domestic inflationary problem."
At 0750 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7045/50 marks, up almost a pfennig from 1.6964/69 late Tuesday.
The dollar was underpinned across the board, meantime, by the renewed talk of a U.S. rate rise next week.

In keeping with the comments from Broaddus, sources close to the Fed told Reuters that there is a very good chance of another 25 basis point rise in the 5.50 percent Federal funds target rate when the Federal Open Market Committee meets on May 20.

Dollar/yen underperformed dollar/mark, however, as heavy selling above 119 in Tokyo capped the unit. Traders said there is a growing belief the Japanese authorities are now happy to keep a lid on the dollar at 120 following last week's successful verbal intervention to weaken it from close to 4-1/2-year highs.

The dollar/yen got a brief fillip in Tokyo from news of a 17 percent year-on-year drop in Japan's March current account surplus and rumours, later denied, that a major Japanese bank suffered large losses at its overseas operations.

However, any dollar pop above 119 yen was used as an excuse by traders to sell at better levels. Analysts said the current account picture in the second quarter is now of more interest amid forecasts the surplus has widening again since March.
As a result of dollar/yen's stasis the mark/yen rate slipped lower again below the psychological 70.0 level and is again sizing up Monday's one-year low at 69.64 again.
Elsewhere, sterling rallied strongly in early trading against a generally weaker mark and ahead of the release at 0930 GMT of the UK April unemployment report.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect the jobless total to drop 40,000 during the month.

On Tuesday, the pound firmed after the Bank of England said the recent strength of sterling improved the inflation outlook this year but that another interest rate rise was likely to be necessary to keep a lid on prices further out.
